videos.script:
A server-rendered page arrives finished. Its buttons are there, and they do nothing yet. This lesson is about that moment. {{hydrate}} First the planner learns to hydrate. The server puts its data in the page, and the script takes the page over instead of drawing it again.

{{mismatch}} Then a bug, on purpose. A date shown as a day of the week. The server says Saturday, a browser in São Paulo says Friday, and the script has to decide which page is real. {{window}} Then the window. A click on a button that is visible and not yet working, and you will watch it get lost.

{{cpu}} You will measure what taking over a page costs a slow processor, in the planner and in the four frameworks. {{stream}} And then the other half. A page sent in pieces. The quick part at once, the slow part a second later, in the same response.

{{four}} Next.js and SvelteKit do it in two different ways, and you will see both arrive. {{status}} And the price: once the first byte has gone, the status cannot change.
